artists.biography:
"The Anchoress is the Welsh multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and author Catherine Anne Davies (aka Catherine AD).
The Anchoress is the stage name of Welsh musician/songwriter Catherine Anne Davies, who also records under the nom de plume Catherine A.D. A self-taught multi-instrumentalist, chanteuse, and singer/songwriter specializing in a heady blend of gothic chamber pop and dark atmospheric art rock, Davies has drawn comparisons to PJ Harvey, Nick Cave, Anna Calvi, My Brightest Diamond, and Kate Bush. She issued a series of well-received independently released EPs before switching over to the Anchoress moniker in 2014 and issuing the single "One for Sorrow.. ~ James Christopher Monger
From March to Dec 2015, Davies performed in Simple Minds' live band, contributing additional guitar and keyboards. She met Jim Kerr through The Dark Flowers collective. She has also performed live with Ed Harcourt at Glastonbury Festival, as well as Martha Wainwright.
Davies has been described by NPR's Ann Powers as "Wales's (much more explicitly feminist) answer to Lana Del Rey."

perplexity.description:
The One For Sorrow EP, released in November 2014 via Hiraeth Records, is an early showcase of The Anchoress’s distinctive blend of art rock and atmospheric pop. Musically, the EP features lush arrangements, introspective lyrics, and a moody, cinematic quality that would become hallmarks of her work. The centerpiece is the original non-album mix of “Long Year,” produced by Gareth Jones, which highlights The Anchoress’s emotive vocals and layered instrumentation, drawing comparisons to artists like Kate Bush and Tori Amos.

As one of The Anchoress’s first major releases, the One For Sorrow EP served as a precursor to her acclaimed debut album, Confessions of a Romance Novelist (2016), establishing her reputation for sophisticated songwriting and genre-blurring soundscapes. The EP was released in limited 12” vinyl, CD, and digital formats, with a special edition including a romance novel, reflecting her conceptual approach. While it did not achieve mainstream commercial success, the EP was well-received by critics and fans, earning praise for its artistic ambition and emotional depth, and solidifying The Anchoress’s place in the UK’s alternative rock scene.
